analyticalQuestion: Can one fixed compact target annulus of a genuine smooth unforced NSE trajectory return to zero at three prescribed positive times, and how do its jet atoms scale along the local recurrence curve?
takeaway: The finite modular lattice re-shoots three simple prescribed returns, a separate cutoff-36 implementation reproduces the parameters and slopes, and five small-curve samples exhibit the analytic quadratic atom-collapse boundary.
nonColorEncoding: filled atom and open first-jet identity markers

panels.A: real and imaginary target traces at three prescribed roots, with nonzero slopes
panels.B: three local directed complex-plane origin passages
panels.C: five re-shot p1 cases, O(p1^2) atom collapse, and exact J=P/4 first-jet identity
panels.D: cutoff residual and slope convergence, independent sparse reshoot, and analytic modular gap annotation

claimBoundary: The traces, roots, fits, and cutoff comparison are finite Fourier-lattice corroboration. The exact 2.5D NSE reduction, modular annulus isolation, recurrence IFT, and second-time-jet packing theorem are analytic results and are not proved by this figure.
